item.title: Idea for possible GAW SCP/ GOI format for GAW
item.content:encoded: Edit: whoops, realized this should go in the ideas forum, sorry bout that. So I don't know if either of these ideas exists already, but I couldn't find either. I have this idea for an SCP made by GAW that is called Meme, which is a memetic that will randomly play memes into your brain, being all you can think about until it goes away in about a day. It gets spread by sharing one of the memes that were a part of the meme onslaught. I also thought that a GAW format for anomalies they create could be rather interesting. In my mind, it would be a chat group, where a member explains their creation, and others comment on and encourage the creation. In essence, it is their way of letting the group know what they made. I know they don't sign their works as GAW, but it would make sense that they in some way share the joke. For instance, with my meme idea, the creator could hit the group with his SCP, and they spread it to other people. I think it would be an interesting narrative, given the narrative of GAW, and would like to write this if others agree that this is a pretty cool idea.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Gamers Against Weed is a satirical name. bluntfiend is even seen stating that they smoke weed, hence the username they used for themselves.

I do not think the 'weed' part is a direct anything in relation to politics. If you look at the tales, they are memers, yes, but they don't exactly attack people, especially not based on political standpoints.

The only thing they seem to make fun of is Dr. Wondertainment with their collection of mister parodies.

So, as far as I'm aware, this group has nothing to do with politics in any way, shape, nor form, as that would be bad taste for the wiki. I think they're just supposed to be a relatable group of IRC chat teens that likes to have fun with anomalies.

item.title: Fun fact

item.title: Re: stuff
item.content:encoded:
They're very similar to the Doctor Wondertainment Misters. As in, they names are there to hint at what they may possibly be. The name "Mr. Original Character" ended up inspiring the format screw involving a personnel file, "Mr. Get Anything For Free In the Shop" ended up mocking online advertisements, and "Mr. Deadly Sins" was interpreted as an entity that exposes immoral online activity. Really, when it comes to Misters Against Weed, the sky is the limit in terms of having fun with the interpretations.

Or you could make something entirely new, like Mr. Doggo.
